label: HiveQL Fundamentals & Architecture
desc: 15 interview questions covering Fundamentals, Architecture, SerDe, Ecosystem and more.

subs.label: Fundamentals
subs.desc: HBase is a NoSQL database that supports record-level update, insert, and delete, but has no built-in SQL-like query language — Hive can be layered on top of HBase for querying.

subs.label: Architecture
subs.desc: What are the main components of Hive? What are the main components of the Query Processor in Apache Hive?

subs.label: SerDe
subs.desc: What is the need for a custom SerDe? What are the different SerDe implementations in Hive?

subs.label: Ecosystem
subs.desc: What is the use of HCatalog? What is the data model of HCatalog?

subs.label: Performance
subs.desc: Setting hive.exec.mode.local.auto to true tells Hive to try fetching query results locally instead of launching a MapReduce job, which is useful for small queries where job start-up overhead would dominate the runtime.

label: Metastore, Data Types & Data Model
desc: 7 interview questions covering Metastore, Data Types.

subs.label: Metastore
subs.desc: The metastore is a relational database that stores Hive's metadata: table definitions, column mappings, partitions, databases, and other schema information.

subs.label: Data Types
subs.desc: Schema-on-read means the schema is validated against the data at query time, not enforced when the data is written.

label: DDL, Tables, Views & Partitioning
desc: 21 interview questions covering DDL, Views, Bucketing, Performance and more.

subs.label: DDL
subs.desc: PURGE is used when you're certain you want to permanently delete a table's data: With PURGE, the data skips the trash folder entirely, so it can't be recovered if the DROP turns out to have been accidental.

subs.label: Views
subs.desc: Can we use the same name for a TABLE and a VIEW in Hive? Can we load data into a VIEW in Hive?

subs.label: Bucketing
subs.desc: Bucketing divides a dataset into a fixed, manageable number of parts based on the hash of a column — conceptually similar to hashing.

subs.label: Performance
subs.desc: A skewed table is a table where some values in a column occur far more often than others, producing a skewed distribution.

subs.label: Tables
subs.desc: A managed table is one whose files, metadata, and statistics are all controlled by Hive's internal processes — this is the default table type Hive creates.

subs.label: Partitioning
subs.desc: How do you prevent data from being dropped or queried from a partition in Hive? What is the use of TOUCH in an ALTER statement?

label: HiveQL Queries, Functions & Joins
desc: 12 interview questions covering Query Syntax, Functions, Optimization, Joins.

subs.label: Query Syntax
subs.desc: SORT BY — sorts data within each reducer; multiple reducers can be used, so the result is only locally sorted per reducer, not globally.

subs.label: Functions
subs.desc: A Generic UDF is a user-defined function written in Java to cover functionality not available in Hive's built-in function set.

subs.label: Optimization
subs.desc: Put the smallest table first and the largest table last in the JOIN — Hive's join execution is optimized to stream the last (largest) table rather than buffer it in memory.

subs.label: Joins
subs.desc: Is it possible to create a Cartesian join between two tables using Hive?

label: Configuration, Sessions & Operations
desc: 17 interview questions covering Configuration, Operations, Performance, File Formats and more.

subs.label: Configuration
subs.desc: What is the use of the .hiverc file in Hive? What is the precedence order for Hive configuration properties?

subs.label: Operations
subs.desc: How do you run Unix shell commands from Hive? What is the purpose of the USE command in Hive?

subs.label: Performance
subs.desc: What is the use of strict mode in Hive? What optimization can be done for a SELECT * query in Hive?

subs.label: File Formats
subs.desc: ORC (Optimized Row Columnar) is a file format built for efficient storage, reading, writing, and processing in Hive.

subs.label: Data Types
subs.desc: Yes — the TIMESTAMP data type stores date/time values, backed by java.sql.Timestamp format.

subs.label: Architecture
subs.desc: Which Java classes handle record encoding for reading and writing Hive table files?
